title: New class nonlocal-oscillators, negative screen: a 2D field of identical Kuramoto-Sakaguchi oscillators with nonlocal coupling goes to plane waves (alpha <= 1.1), spiral turbulence with incoherent filaments (1.2-1.3) or global incoherence (>= 1.4); no discrete, persistent incoherent spots (chimera bodies) from random or smooth initial phases
summary: world.py: d phi/dt = -K Im(e^{i(phi+alpha)} conj(G * e^{i phi})), Gaussian kernel of width R, 128^2 periodic, dt 0.1, identical oscillators, no noise (fuel coupling present but off). A body would be a localized domain of low local coherence 1-|Z|. screen.py (seed 0, 300-1500 t): random phases at alpha 1.45 R 6 stay incoherent everywhere (95-98% of the box above 0.3); smooth random phases at alpha 0.6, 0.9 and 1.1 (R 6) pass through spirals whose cores are incoherent dots (alpha1.1_R6.png t=100-300) and end in a coherent plane wave by t=400; at alpha 1.2 and 1.25 (R 6, to t=1500) and 1.3 the field stays in spiral turbulence whose incoherence forms filaments and blobs that are born and vanish (2-7 connected regions, 56-80% of the box); at alpha 1.4 R 16 and 1.2 R 12 the same turbulence on a larger scale.

finding.operator: nonlocal Kuramoto-Sakaguchi phase coupling (chimera model) on a 2D field
finding.control: alpha scan 0.6-1.45 at R 6, R 12 and 16, random vs smooth initial phases, seed 0
finding.result: alpha <= 1.1: plane wave by t=400; 1.2-1.3: spiral turbulence, incoherent filaments, 2-7 regions, no persistent spots; >= 1.4: incoherent nearly everywhere

limits: One seed, short runs (300-1500 t), seven parameter points, identical frequencies and no noise; spot chimeras in the literature need tuned initial conditions (a planted incoherent patch), which would not count as S, and I did not try them, the fuel-coupled variant (fuel 1), a top-hat kernel or larger boxes. The incoherent spiral cores at alpha 1.1 are the closest thing to bodies and live ~200 t before the plane wave wins.
